subject: MSA & Order Form - Term, Auto‑Renew, and Exit Mechanics

Subject: MSA & Order Form - Term, Auto‑Renew, and Exit Mechanics

Rishi / Karthik —

Thanks for walking us through the platform last week. Procurement ran the latest MSA + order form by our legal team and returned comments focused primarily on the Term and Termination sections. High-level asks:

- No automatic one‑year renewals without a notice window longer than 30 days (they want 60–90).
- Carve out a limited termination for convenience on the order form (Acme may need to decommit for product strategy reasons).
- Clear export and transfer obligations (30 days) and a pro‑rated refund for unused committed capacity.

I attached our redlines (Acme_MSA_comments.docx). Can Redwood legal propose a single paragraph that covers: notice windows, auto‑renew mechanics, and an order‑form termination-for-convenience fee/cure?

We'd like to close commercial terms this week if possible — can you confirm next steps and timing?

Thanks,
Jordan Peters
Procurement, Acme Cloud Solutions
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Peters <jpeters@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 11:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA & Order Form - Term, Auto‑Renew, and Exit Mechanics

Jordan —

Appreciate the clear summary and the redlines. Quick commercial response from our side:

- We can be flexible on the notice window — proposing a 60‑day written notice to terminate before an automatic renewal.
- For termination for convenience on the order form, we can agree to a customer‑initiated termination with a 30‑day cure and a one‑time transition fee equal to 10% of the remaining committed monthly fees (to cover reserved capacity).
- We will commit to a 30‑day assistance window for data export and a pro‑rata refund for unused committed months.

I'll loop in legal to convert this into redline language. Laura / Karthik — can you propose specific clause text (two options: conservative/legal preferred and sales‑friendly)? Jordan, if those concessions sound acceptable in principle, I can escalate to get a final sign‑off today.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA & Order Form - Term, Auto‑Renew, and Exit Mechanics

Folks —

Draft language (commercial option and legal preferred option below). I kept the concepts consolidated so we can pick one approach and apply to both MSA (term mechanics) and Order Form (TFC).

Option A — Sales‑friendly (single paragraph on Order Form):
"Customer may terminate this Order Form for convenience upon sixty (60) days' prior written notice to Redwood. Upon such termination, (i) Customer will pay a termination fee equal to ten percent (10%) of the remaining unpaid committed fees for the then‑current term, and (ii) Redwood will provide reasonable assistance to export Customer data for thirty (30) days following termination and will refund any prepaid, unused committed fees on a pro‑rata basis." 

Option B — Legal preferred (MSA + Order Form split):
MSA (Auto‑renew): "Each Order Form shall have the Term set forth therein. Unless either party provides written notice of non‑renewal at least ninety (90) days prior to the end of the then‑current Term, the Order Form will automatically renew for successive one (1) year terms at Redwood's published list price unless otherwise agreed in writing." 

Order Form (TFC): "Customer may terminate an Order Form for convenience only if Customer provides at least sixty (60) days' prior written notice and pays a termination fee equal to twenty percent (20%) of the remaining committed fees for the then‑current Term. Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to assist with data export for thirty (30) days; any prepaid, unused fees will be refunded on a pro‑rata basis." 

Questions for Laura: which option exposes us to greater capacity risk? Can we narrow the data assistance obligation (e.g., support hours cap) while keeping sales moving?

Karthik
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 08:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA & Order Form - Term, Auto‑Renew, and Exit Mechanics

Thanks — reviewed both options. Legal notes below (summary):

- Option A (sales‑friendly) is customer‑friendly and faster for close but offers limited protection for Redwood when customers terminate large reserved pools. Consider a transition cap (e.g., assistance limited to 40 hours or X GB of export throughput) and a minimum termination fee floor (e.g., $5,000) for small deals.
- Option B (legal preferred) is safer but the 90‑day auto‑renew notice is on the longer side for enterprise procurement; we could compromise at 75 days for mutuality.
- Suggest redline tweaks: replace "commercially reasonable efforts" with "reasonable assistance as described in the Service Level Annex" and add a clause that refunds will exclude non‑refundable third‑party costs and pass‑through charges.

Proposed compromise language to put in the document that balances risk:
"Customer may terminate an Order Form for convenience upon sixty (60) days' prior written notice. Customer shall pay a termination fee equal to the greater of (a) ten percent (10%) of the remaining unpaid committed fees for the then‑current Term, or (b) five thousand dollars ($5,000). Redwood will provide reasonable assistance to export Customer data for thirty (30) days following termination (capped at forty (40) hours of engineering support unless otherwise agreed). Any prepaid, unused committed fees will be refunded on a pro‑rata basis, excluding non‑refundable third‑party costs." 

If sales is comfortable with the cap and minimum fee, I can insert this into a redline PDF and send to Acme.

—Laura
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Peters <jpeters@acmecloud.com>

Subject: Re: MSA & Order Form - Term, Auto‑Renew, and Exit Mechanics

Rishi / Team —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and for proposing middle ground. Acme can accept the 60‑day termination notice and the 30‑day export assistance if Redwood will: (a) agree to the $5,000 minimum termination fee for smaller pilots, and (b) refund pro‑rata unused committed months. We also request that the export support cap be expressed as "up to 40 hours of engineering support or reasonable export throughput at no additional charge" so we have clarity on expectations.

If you can slot that into the Order Form redline, we can sign the PO and return a signed copy (attached: Acme_Signed_PO.pdf).

Jordan
